title: Spin on a relaxed load in the stripe steal loop's exit check
body:
# PR Details

## Description

Stack 25/39, on top of #134. Follow-up to the 2026-10-18 cleanup audit.

- Under TSAN, each acquire atomic load locks the atomic's sync object; ~100 workers spinning on `activeStripes.load(acquire)` starved the single `fetch_sub(release)` that retires the last stripe, hanging parallel_for (~20% of runs on 112 cores).
- New `allStripesRetired()` spins on a relaxed load and performs one acquire load once it reads 0; by read-read coherence that load also reads 0, so it synchronizes with all release decrements as before.
- Zero-cost in normal builds (one extra load on exit); no TSAN-only `#if` needed, and no sleep/yield backoff introduced.

## Test Plan

- clang TSAN (RelWithDebInfo, -fsanitize=thread), `chunked_for_test --gtest_filter=ChunkedFor.SimpleLoopAuto` one process per run, 60 s timeout. Before: 4/20 hung (plus 2 more within ~20 further tries while capturing backtraces). After: 0/60.
- Backtrace of a hang (gdb): all 113 threads in runStripeWorker; the main thread blocked in __sanitizer::FutexWait under __tsan_atomic32_fetch_sub (the final activeStripes release decrement) while the others spin on __tsan_atomic32_load(acquire).
- TSAN ctest -R "for|Chunked|parallel": 61/61 pass. GCC C++14 Release full ctest -LE flaky: 1287/1287 pass.

The regrouped stack was verified locally at every PR boundary (GCC 14 Release build of library, tests, examples and benchmarks; `ctest -LE flaky` all pass) and at its tip under ASAN+UBSAN (C++14) and Clang TSAN (all pass), with Doxygen 1.11.0 warning-free. CI's 4-vCPU pool size can't be reproduced locally; CI covers it.

## Types of changes

- [ ] Docs change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature

## Stable surface

- [ ] Adds to the stable surface, without changing compatibility or behaviour for existing documented use
- [ ] Alters or removes something present in the most recent tagged release
- [ ] Alters or removes something added since that release, and not yet shipped

- [ ] Public API or ABI
- [ ] Default behaviour
- [ ] A documented concurrency guarantee — ordering, forward progress, cancellation, lifetime or safety

none. Internal detail header (detail/par_for_stripe.h); no API/ABI change; the memory-ordering guarantee of the termination check is preserved (acquire still performed before returning).

files.patch:
@@ -30,6 +30,7 @@ Unreleased
 * On Windows, dispenso headers no longer leave `_AMD64_`/`_X86_`/`_ARM64_`/`_ARM_` defined in user code, and no longer define `_X86_` alongside an existing `_AMD64_` when `<windows.h>` was included first.
 * `graph.h` no longer declares `callFunctor`, `destroyFunctor` and `ExecutorBase` in a global `detail` namespace, which broke compilation of user code that has its own `::detail` names.
 * Language-version checks now use `_MSVC_LANG` on MSVC (via the new `DISPENSO_CPLUSPLUS` macro), so MSVC builds with `/std:c++17` or later get the C++17/C++20 features (std::optional in `AsyncRequest` and pipelines, C++20 concept constraints, `[[deprecated]]` warnings) without needing `/Zc:__cplusplus`.
+* `parallel_for` with adaptive chunking no longer hangs intermittently under ThreadSanitizer on many-core machines. This was an interaction with the TSAN runtime, where spinning workers starved the final completion update; normal builds were unaffected.
 
 ### Documentation
 * The API reference now includes `dispenso/utils/graph_dot.h` and `graphsToDot`, listed under the Graph topic.
